claims.text: Minor alloying with 1–2 at.% Ti or Al followed by heat treatment will induce nanoscale coherent precipitates in a MoNbTaW refractory HEA matrix.
The induced coherent precipitates will be uniformly distributed within the HEA matrix.
The precipitates will interact with dislocations and enhance strain hardening.
Precipitate–dislocation interactions will promote uniform deformation.
Maintaining precipitate coherence will prevent embrittlement.
Coherent precipitates will preserve the alloy's high strength.
Minor alloying and precipitation will not significantly alter matrix composition or phase stability.
Preserving matrix composition and phase stability will maintain the impact-induced energetic response.
The precipitate-containing alloy will have more than a 20% increase in elongation to failure relative to the untreated baseline.
The precipitate-containing alloy will have a higher strain-hardening exponent than the untreated baseline.
The yield strength of the precipitate-containing alloy will remain within 10% of the untreated baseline.
The precipitate-containing alloy will retain the impact-induced energy release of the untreated baseline.
The proposed benefits will hold from room temperature through moderate temperatures up to 800 °C.
The proposed benefits will hold under both quasi-static and dynamic loading relevant to energetic structural applications.
The untreated refractory HEA baseline has high strength but limited ductility and uniform deformability.
An excessively high precipitate fraction may cause embrittlement and diminish the benefit.
Loss of precipitate coherence may diminish the benefit.
The effect depends on the refractory alloy system and precipitate chemistry.
